title: Affine morphisms and affine scalar extension preserve first-cohomology vanishing
statement: Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space], quasi-compact and quasi-separated, meaning that its point space is quasi-compact and its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and cohomology $H^q=R^q\Gamma$ of underlying additive sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Suppose $H^1(X,F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $F$. Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and let $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ induce the identity on global functions [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An affine morphism of algebraic spaces means a representable morphism whose scheme base changes are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. (1) For every affine morphism $f:Y\to X$, the space $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $H^1(Y,G)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $G$. (2) For every unital ring map $A\to A\prime$, put $X\prime=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A\prime$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The projection $X\prime\to X$ is affine, the space $X\prime$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, its diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}A\prime$ is quasi-compact, and the canonical map $$A\prime\longrightarrow\Gamma(X\prime,\mathcal O_{X\prime})$$ induced by $X\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}A\prime$ is an isomorphism of rings. The zero ring and empty spaces are allowed.

proof.text: First compare the two readings of quasi-compactness. For an algebraic space, a quasi-compact point space gives an affine, hence quasi-compact, representable surjective etale scheme chart [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]; conversely the target of such a chart from a quasi-compact scheme has quasi-compact point space [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas]. Applied to a space and to the pullbacks of its absolute diagonal along affine scheme tests, which are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], this shows that the chart notions of quasi-compact and quasi-separated in [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] agree with the point-space notions of the statement and of [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence]. For (1), [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] gives that $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For quasi-coherent $G$ on $Y$, [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-base-change] says that $f_*G$ is quasi-coherent. The additive-sheaf cohomology comparison [lem-sfb-space-affine-cohomology], with $q=1$, identifies $H^1(Y,G)$ with $H^1(X,f_*G)$. The latter is zero by the hypothesis on $X$. This proves all of (1).

proof.text: Write $Z=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ and $q:Z'\to Z$, with $f:X'\to X$ and $p':X'\to Z'$ the projections. Every affine scheme test $\operatorname{Spec}B\to Z$ has fibre product $\operatorname{Spec}(A'\otimes_A B)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Thus $q$ is affine by the scheme-test definition; its base change $f$ is affine by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. That node also gives that $X'$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated in its chart sense, hence in the point-space sense by the comparison of step 1 through [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] and [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas]. The affine scheme $Z'$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] applied to $p':X'\to Z'$ gives that $p'$ is quasi-separated. This is exactly the requested quasi-compactness of its relative diagonal.

source.place: Tag 07V0(2), first sentence; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03WI (lemma-base-change-affine) and 073B (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence).

proof.text: On an affine etale scheme test $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\to Z$, [lem-trf-space-chart-limit-enlarged-sections] identifies $(q_*\mathcal O_{Z'})(V)$ with the regular functions on $Z'\times_ZV$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] these functions are $A'\otimes_A B$; $a'\in A'$ pulls back to $a'\otimes1$. On the other hand [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] give the very same values and pure-tensor pullback maps for $\widetilde{A'}_{\mathrm{et}}$, as defined in [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. These formulas commute with every ring map of affine etale tests. Restriction and the sheaf gluing axiom therefore give $q_*\mathcal O_{Z'}\simeq\widetilde{A'}_{\mathrm{et}}$, preserving $a'\mapsto a'\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 07V0(2), identification of the affine direct-image algebra before applying Tag 07U8; explicit affine-test calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-base-change] to the affine morphism $q:Z'\to Z$, the base change $p:X\to Z$, and $\mathcal O_{Z'}$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $p^*q_*\mathcal O_{Z'}\xrightarrow{\sim}f_*p'^*\mathcal O_{Z'}$, and $p'^*\mathcal O_{Z'}\simeq\mathcal O_{X'}\otimes_{p'^{-1}\mathcal O_{Z'}}p'^{-1}\mathcal O_{Z'}=\mathcal O_{X'}$ by the tensor-pullback identification of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization], so the target is $f_*\mathcal O_{X'}$. After step 3 the source is $p^*\widetilde{A'}_{\mathrm{et}}=A'\otimes_A\mathcal O_X$. With $M=A'$, [lem-sfb-space-acyclic-global-module-sections] now gives a bijection $A'\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,A'\otimes_A\mathcal O_X)$. Compose with global sections of the preceding sheaf isomorphism and the defining equality $\Gamma(X,f_*\mathcal O_{X'})=\Gamma(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$.

source.place: Tag 07V0(2), final displayed calculation, using Tags 07U8 (lemma-affine-base-change) and 07UZ (lemma-vanishing-compute).

proof.text: For $a'\in A'$, the map in step 4 first gives $a'\otimes1$. By the defining counit formula for the canonical base-change map in [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-base-change] and the local tensor formula of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization], its image is the pullback of $a'$ along $p':X'\to Z'$. Consequently the bijection just proved is the canonical ring homomorphism in (2), hence is a ring isomorphism. No step excludes $A'=0$ or $X=\varnothing$: spectra, tensor products, direct images and the cited module computation all include these cases.
